messages:
Andrew Chen: RFC follow-up — SDK transport + retries + pagination. Wanted to capture quick decisions so we can update the RFC and package owners.
Sarah Li: high level: keep the public SDK surface consistent across languages. Implementation can differ per runtime, but API shape should be obvious and small.
Mike Patel: +1. Main tradeoffs left: gRPC vs HTTP/JSON for streaming and pub/sub style responses, binary vs json payloads, and where to put retry logic (client vs transport).
Olivia Gomez: devex note: users care most about simple defaults that 'just work' in browser and server. Complexity ok behind flags.
Andrew Chen: proposal draft:
```
- Python: default to httpx with HTTP/2 where available. expose streaming via async iterator.
- TS: use fetch + readable streams for browser; node uses undici/http2 if available. No native gRPC in browser by default.
- Go: prefer gRPC + protobuf streaming for lowest CPU overhead; provide a thin JSON-over-HTTP compatibility layer for customers who need it.
- Retry policy: SDK exposes a RetryConfig (max_attempts, backoff_strategy, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter) with sane defaults. Idempotency key support for non-idempotent calls.
- Pagination: do not auto-iterate by default in any SDK. Provide helpers: paginator that can be opt-in (auto_paginate: false by default).
```
Sarah Li: question: for TS/node, are we comfortable supporting http2 in both node 18+ and undici? falling back to http1.1 is fine but streaming semantics differ.
Mike Patel: node http2 and undici both exist; prefer undici for perf but it doesn't do http2 by default. We should detect and switch. Also grpc-web exists — could be used for browser streaming but adds build/dependency complexity.
Olivia Gomez: user story: a React dev who just wants streaming text tokens should be able to adopt SDK with one import and zero build config. So grpc-web + custom bundling is a blocker.
Andrew Chen: decision: no grpc-web for browser. TS will use fetch + ReadableStream and a small framing protocol for token streaming (similar to SSE but over fetch). Node will use undici/http2 when available.
Mike Patel: for Go, gRPC first makes sense. But include an http-json shim so server-to-server integrations that can't do gRPC can still call easily.
Sarah Li: retries: we need transparent retries for idempotent routes (embeddings, read-only). For generation endpoints with streaming, retrying is tricky. Propose: streaming endpoints do not retry mid-stream. Instead SDK should surface a retry-on-start option — if connection fails before any tokens, auto-retry. After first token, fail and surface partial stream.
Andrew Chen: agreed. We'll document this and include 'max_start_retries' config separate from normal retries.
Olivia Gomez: pagination helpers: show example patterns in docs rather than hiding them. Provide an "AutoPaginator" helper in Python and TS that must be explicitly imported and called.
Mike Patel: example API names:
- Python: client.generate(...)
         for page in client.list_items.paginate(...):
             ...
  plus client.list_items.get_all(...) (explicit convenience that fetches all pages and warns about cost)
- TS: client.list.items({auto_paginate: false}) returns {items, next_cursor}
      client.list.items.autoPaginate({}) returns async iterable (opt-in)

Sarah Li: also think about telemetry: if user calls get_all() we should emit an event so billing/console show that this did many requests.
Andrew Chen: good. Add metrics: pagination_pages, auto_pagination_used
Olivia Gomez: docs + migration: add code snippets for common use-cases and a migration guide from older SDKs.
Mike Patel: small nit: default retry counts: 3 attempts total, backoff starting 100ms, max 2s, full jitter. Make these constants in each SDK.
Andrew Chen: noted. I'll update the RFC with these concrete defaults and the language-specific transports. Action items:
- @Sarah Li: write up TS transport detection and fetch/undici fallback (issue)
- @Mike Patel: draft Go gRPC + http shim api shape
- @Olivia Gomez: docs snippets for streaming & pagination patterns
- @Andrew Chen: update RFC and include retry semantics paragraph and default constants
deploy-bot: created issue #3421 for 'TS transport detection' (assign: Sarah Li)
Sarah Li: I'll take #3421. Will sketch detection pseudo-code and note bundlers' caveats.
Andrew Chen: thanks all. I'll post updated RFC in a few hours.
